verdicts.reading: Iran's nuclear standoff and regional role make 2007 a highly unstable year in the Middle East with Iran at the centre.
verdicts.mainstream_test: In calendar 2007 the Iran nuclear standoff escalated materially (sanctions, confrontation, conflict) with documented effect.
verdicts.reason: The standoff escalated in part: UNSC Resolution 1747 (March 2007) widened sanctions. But no military conflict involving Iran occurred and the December 2007 US NIE (weapons work halted in 2003) lowered the urgency. Regional instability was real (Iraq, Gaza) but not driven mainly by an Iran crisis.

evidence.title: Nuclear program of Iran (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: UNSC 1747 broadened sanctions in March 2007; the December 2007 NIE judged Iran had halted its weapons program in 2003, which reduced urgency.

verdicts.reading: Nigeria's 2007 presidential election seriously strains its democratic system.
verdicts.mainstream_test: The 2007 election was widely judged seriously flawed or destabilising, with documented effect.
verdicts.reason: The April 2007 election was condemned by EU observers as falling far short of international standards, with rampant rigging, violence and ballot theft; opposition rejected the result and petitioned the courts.

evidence.title: 2007 Nigerian presidential election (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: EU observers: fraud, violence, disenfranchisement; described by observers as among the worst they had seen; results contested in court.

verdicts.reading: Iraq and US policy there stay in bad shape in 2007, risking state collapse and wider sectarian war.
verdicts.mainstream_test: In 2007 Iraq saw state collapse or a widening sectarian war, or at least sustained severe deterioration.
verdicts.reason: Violence was severe in the first half of 2007 (over 1,700 civilian deaths in May; US deaths peaked at 126 in May), so 'bad shape' held. But the state did not collapse and sectarian war did not widen; violence fell sharply in the second half after the surge.

evidence.title: Iraq War troop surge of 2007 (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Civilian deaths fell from over 1,700 in May 2007 to about 500 in December; the Iraqi state kept functioning.

verdicts.reading: Turkey's two 2007 elections expose divisions and test the country's stability.
verdicts.mainstream_test: The 2007 Turkish elections produced a documented political crisis.
verdicts.reason: The presidential election triggered the military's 27 April e-memorandum, mass secularist rallies, a Constitutional Court annulment and a snap general election in July before Gul was elected in August.

evidence.title: 2007 Turkish presidential election (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: E-memorandum 27 April, court annulment 1 May, rallies of over a million, early election 22 July, Gul elected 28 August.

verdicts.reading: Russia becomes riskier in 2007 through assertive petro-confident foreign policy and succession manoeuvring.
verdicts.mainstream_test: In 2007 Russia took documented assertive steps and the succession contest played out.
verdicts.reason: Putin's Munich speech (February), CFE treaty suspension (July) and missile-defence dispute marked an assertive turn; the succession was manoeuvred with Medvedev named in December 2007 and Putin set to become prime minister.

evidence.title: Munich speech of Vladimir Putin (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Speech attacking unipolar order; CFE suspension in July 2007.

evidence.title: 2008 Russian presidential election (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Putin named Medvedev successor on 10 December 2007, with Putin to become prime minister.

verdicts.reading: Elite tension rises in China around the fall 2007 Party Congress as Hu consolidates power.
verdicts.mainstream_test: The 17th Party Congress or 2007 elite politics showed documented conflict or instability.
verdicts.reason: The 17th Congress was orderly and predictable; Hu consolidated through his ideology entering the constitution and Zeng Qinghong's retirement, with no documented elite conflict of material effect.

evidence.title: 17th National Congress of the CCP (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: No significant elite conflict; outcomes negotiated in advance; Xi and Li elevated; smooth transition set up.

verdicts.reading: Musharraf faces a political storm in 2007 that weakens him or forces him out.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Musharraf was materially weakened or removed in 2007.
verdicts.reason: The judicial crisis, the November 3 emergency, his forced resignation as army chief on November 28 and Bhutto's assassination on December 27 left him badly weakened; he resigned the presidency in August 2008.

evidence.title: 2007 Pakistani state of emergency (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Emergency declared, judges refused oath, Musharraf quit as army chief on 28 November, Bhutto assassinated 27 December.

verdicts.reading: The Taiwan issue stays calm in 2007.
verdicts.mainstream_test: No cross-strait crisis with documented material effect occurred in 2007.
verdicts.reason: Chen Shui-bian's UN-referendum push raised rhetoric but there was no military or economic crisis; relations improved in 2008.

evidence.title: Cross-Strait relations (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: No major crisis documented in 2007-2008; talks resumed in 2008.

verdicts.reading: North Korea does not cause serious trouble in 2007.
verdicts.mainstream_test: No nuclear test, missile crisis or military clash by North Korea in 2007.
verdicts.reason: 2007 saw the February 13 agreement and the Yongbyon shutdown verified by the IAEA in July; no nuclear or missile tests until 2009.

evidence.title: Six-party talks (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: February 2007 agreement; Yongbyon shutdown verified 18 July 2007; no tests in 2007-2008.

verdicts.reading: Latin America does not cause serious political or market trouble in 2007.
verdicts.mainstream_test: No regional crisis (default, coup, major conflict) with documented material effect in 2007.
verdicts.reason: No coup, default or regional crisis occurred; Chavez's December 2007 constitutional referendum was rejected and the result accepted.

evidence.title: 2009 Venezuelan constitutional referendum (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Notes the 2007 reform proposal was rejected by voters, a peaceful outcome.

verdicts.reading: Southeast Asia does not cause serious trouble in 2007.
verdicts.mainstream_test: No major political crisis in Southeast Asia with documented material effect in 2007.
verdicts.reason: Thailand returned to elections in December 2007, but Myanmar's Saffron Revolution (largest protests in 20 years, 13-31 deaths, new US and EU sanctions) was a significant regional crisis, though without wider market effect.

evidence.title: 2007 Burmese anti-government protests (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Protests of up to 100,000 in Yangon, crackdown with 13-31 deaths, new Western sanctions.

verdicts.reading: Saudi Arabia does not cause serious trouble in 2007.
verdicts.mainstream_test: No destabilising attack, unrest or succession crisis in Saudi Arabia in 2007.
verdicts.reason: One attack killed four French nationals and hundreds of suspects were arrested, but the insurgency had subsided after 2004-05 and the state was stable.

evidence.title: Insurgency in Saudi Arabia (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: One attack (26 February 2007, four killed) and mass arrests; attacks had decreased dramatically since late 2004.

verdicts.reading: Large aid inflows start to make a meaningful difference in some of Africa's least developed states in 2007.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Documented measurable improvement attributable to aid in some least developed African states by 2007.
verdicts.reason: WHO-led analysis found that after nationwide aid-funded bednet and ACT scale-up by 2007, child malaria deaths fell by about 67% in Rwanda and 62% in Ethiopia. That is a meaningful aid effect in some states.

evidence.title: Initial evidence of reduction of malaria cases and deaths in Rwanda and Ethiopia (Malaria Journal)
evidence.shows: In-patient malaria deaths in under-5s fell 67% (Rwanda) and 62% (Ethiopia) after LLIN and ACT scale-up completed by 2007.

verdicts.reading: US policymaking (Bush administration and Congress) moves toward increased protectionism in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: In 2008 the US adopted or blocked trade measures in a documented protectionist shift (new tariffs or barriers, trade deals blocked).
verdicts.reason: Congress did not approve the pending Colombia FTA in 2008, and anti-trade rhetoric marked the campaign. But no major new tariffs or protectionist law passed in 2008; Buy American provisions came only in 2009. So the shift happened in part.

evidence.title: Colombia Trade Promotion Agreement (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: The agreement was not approved by Congress before the end of the 2008 session; passed only in October 2011.

verdicts.reading: The Iran standoff stays dangerous in 2008, with the US pushing sanctions and Iran defiant.
verdicts.mainstream_test: In 2008 new sanctions were imposed and Iran kept defying them (continued enrichment).
verdicts.reason: UNSC Resolution 1803 (March 2008) expanded sanctions while Iran continued enrichment; the standoff persisted without strikes, as the summary expected.

evidence.title: Nuclear program of Iran (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Resolution 1803 further expanded sanctions against Iran's continuing nuclear activities.

verdicts.reading: Frustration with stalled politics jeopardises Iraq's central government in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: In 2008 Iraq's central government was materially weakened or threatened by political deadlock.
verdicts.reason: The central government grew stronger: the Basra operation in March 2008 consolidated Maliki's authority with cross-sectarian support, and parliament passed the US status of forces agreement in late 2008.

evidence.title: Battle of Basra (2008) (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Strategic victory for the government; strengthened Maliki's central authority with Kurdish and Sunni backing.

verdicts.reading: A mass-casualty terror attack by Al Qaeda or allied groups is a substantial risk in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: A mass-casualty attack (dozens or more killed) by Al Qaeda or allied jihadist groups occurred in 2008.
verdicts.reason: The Mumbai attacks (November 2008, 166 civilians killed) by Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba and the Islamabad Marriott bombing (September 2008, 54 killed, US intelligence suspected Al Qaeda or associates) were mass-casualty attacks by allied jihadist groups.

evidence.title: 2008 Mumbai attacks (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: 175 killed in attacks by Lashkar-e-Taiba.

evidence.title: Islamabad Marriott Hotel bombing (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: 54 killed; US intelligence suggested Al Qaeda or its associates.

verdicts.reading: Afghanistan and Pakistan face worsening political and security problems and radicalism in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Documented security deterioration and political turmoil in both countries in 2008.
verdicts.reason: Afghanistan saw its deadliest suicide bombing to date (Kandahar, February) and commanders warned of worsening conditions; Pakistan saw Musharraf's exit, rising US strikes and the Marriott bombing.

evidence.title: 2008 in Afghanistan (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Kandahar bombing killed 100, deadliest of the war to then; McKiernan warned in October the situation could get much worse.

evidence.title: Islamabad Marriott Hotel bombing (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Attack after Musharraf's departure amid rising militancy and US missile strikes.

verdicts.reading: An emboldened Kremlin acts as a spoiler on key international issues in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Russia took documented actions in 2008 that blocked or upended Western-led resolution of international issues.
verdicts.reason: Russia opposed Kosovo's independence, fought the August 2008 war with Georgia and recognised Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

evidence.title: Russo-Georgian War (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: War 1-16 August 2008; Russia recognised Abkhazia and South Ossetia on 26 August; context of opposition to Kosovo independence.

verdicts.reading: South Africa faces a difficult, uncertain 2008 from the Mbeki-Zuma split but largely weathers it.
verdicts.mainstream_test: The Mbeki-Zuma division produced documented political turmoil in 2008 without breakdown.
verdicts.reason: The split produced turmoil beyond the forecast detail: the ANC recalled Mbeki in September 2008 (he did not stay until 2009), but the transition to Motlanthe was constitutional and orderly. The risk materialised and the country weathered it; the detail that Mbeki would stay was wrong.

evidence.title: Thabo Mbeki (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Mbeki resigned at the ANC NEC's request on 20 September 2008; Motlanthe became interim president.

verdicts.reading: The AKP's constitutional plans raise Turkey's risk of political instability in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: In 2008 a documented constitutional or political crisis arose around the AKP's agenda.
verdicts.reason: The AKP's headscarf amendment led to a closure case; on 30 July 2008 the Constitutional Court fell one vote short of banning the ruling party and cut its funding.

evidence.title: 2008 Justice and Development Party closure trial (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Six of eleven judges voted to close the party (seven needed); funding cut by half.

verdicts.reading: Energy underinvestment in Latin America limits the region's growth in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Documented energy shortages in 2008 that constrained economic activity in Latin American countries.
verdicts.reason: Argentina cut gas exports to Chile and supply to about 300 industrial users in May 2008 after years of stagnant output under price controls; Chilean industry cut operations. The effect was limited to some countries, and the 2008-09 slowdown was driven by the global crisis.

evidence.title: Argentina Cuts Chile Gas Exports (Energy Intelligence)
evidence.shows: Argentina halted gas exports to Chile and cut gas to selected industrial users; production stagnant for four years due to price controls.

evidence.title: IEA Energy Policy Review 2009: Chile
evidence.shows: Chile's gas imports from Argentina fell to about 1 Mcm/day in 2008, forcing fuel switching.

verdicts.reading: China remains politically stable in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: No major unrest or instability in China with documented material effect in 2008.
verdicts.reason: The regime was stable and hosted the Olympics, but the March 2008 Tibetan unrest (over 150 protests, 23 to 200+ deaths, heavy troop deployment) was a significant unrest episode.

evidence.title: 2008 Tibetan unrest (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: About 150 protests in two weeks; deaths 23 (official) to 200+; large military deployment.

verdicts.reading: Taiwan remains stable in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: No cross-strait crisis in 2008.
verdicts.reason: Ma Ying-jeou's election in March 2008 led to resumed talks and direct flights in December; no crisis.

evidence.title: Cross-Strait relations (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Talks resumed June 2008; direct flights began 15 December 2008.

verdicts.reading: North Korea is not a source of instability in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: No nuclear test, missile crisis or military clash by North Korea in 2008.
verdicts.reason: No tests in 2008; the US removed North Korea from the terror list in October 2008. Verification disputes stalled talks but caused no crisis.

evidence.title: Six-party talks (Wikipedia)

verdicts.reading: Saudi Arabia remains stable in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: No destabilising attack or unrest in Saudi Arabia in 2008.
verdicts.reason: No terrorist incidents recorded in 2008.

evidence.title: Insurgency in Saudi Arabia (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: No terrorist incidents recorded in 2008.

verdicts.reading: Nigeria is not a source of instability in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: No unrest in Nigeria with documented material effect (e.g. on oil output) in 2008.
verdicts.reason: National politics were stable after the 2007 transfer, but MEND's Niger Delta campaign shut about 10% of national oil output with the June 2008 Bonga attack and waged an 'oil war' in September 2008.

evidence.title: Movement for the Emancipation of the Niger Delta (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Bonga attack 20 June 2008 shut 10% of Nigerian output; Operation Hurricane Barbarossa September 2008.

verdicts.reading: Russia's domestic politics stay stable in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: The 2008 succession passed without unrest or elite rupture.

evidence.title: 2008 Russian presidential election (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Election without major unrest; Medvedev 71.25%; Putin became prime minister.

verdicts.reading: A stronger US Congress assertively drives the economic policy and financial regulation agenda in 2009.
verdicts.mainstream_test: In 2009 Congress wrote and passed major economic and financial-regulation legislation on its own terms.
verdicts.reason: Congress drafted the stimulus (ARRA, February 2009) and the House passed Barney Frank's Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act on 11 December 2009, the basis of Dodd-Frank.

evidence.title: Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act of 2009 (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: House passed the Frank bill 223-202 on 11 December 2009; Congress played the primary role in shaping financial reform.

verdicts.reading: Security in India, Pakistan and Afghanistan deteriorates significantly in 2009 and the US and Europe become more directly involved in all three.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Documented security deterioration in 2009 in each of the three countries, plus deeper Western involvement.
verdicts.reason: Afghanistan deteriorated (IED attacks up 120%, 512 foreign soldiers killed, US surge announced) and Pakistan fought a major Swat war displacing 2 million. India did not deteriorate: terrorism deaths fell from 824 (2008) to 774 with no Mumbai-scale attack, and no Western involvement there. Two of three countries.

evidence.title: Coalition casualties in Afghanistan (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: 7,228 IED attacks in 2009, up 120% from 2008; 512 foreign soldiers killed.

evidence.title: Second Battle of Swat (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Major offensive May-July 2009; 2 million displaced.

evidence.title: List of terrorist incidents in India (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Terrorism deaths 774 in 2009 vs 824 in 2008; no attack on the Mumbai scale.

verdicts.reading: 2009 is the critical year for direct or proxy conflict between Iran and Israel.
verdicts.mainstream_test: In 2009 Iran and Israel clashed directly, or proxy conflict escalated materially.
verdicts.reason: No direct Iran-Israel conflict and no Israeli strike on Iran occurred in 2009. Proxy conflict occurred in part: the Gaza war with Hamas ran to 18 January 2009 (it began before publication) and Israel reportedly struck an Iranian arms shipment for Hamas in Sudan. The central risk did not materialise.

evidence.title: Gaza War (2008-2009) (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: War from 27 December 2008 to 18 January 2009; mentions a reported Israeli strike on an Iranian arms ship for Hamas in Sudan.

evidence.title: Iran-Israel proxy conflict (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: No direct clash or Israeli strike on Iran recorded for 2009.

verdicts.reading: The financial crisis brings increased social unrest in Russia, met with near-zero tolerance, and worse relations with the West in 2009.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Documented rise in crisis-driven protests in Russia in 2009, and a deterioration in relations with the West.
verdicts.reason: Some crisis-driven unrest happened (Pikalyovo highway blockade over wage arrears, which Putin settled in person), but it was small-scale. Relations with the West improved through the US 'reset'. So the risk materialised only in part.

evidence.title: Pikalyovo, Leningrad Oblast (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: About 300 residents blocked a highway over wage delays; Putin ordered Deripaska to pay.

evidence.title: Russia-United States relations (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Relations improved significantly in 2009 through the reset.

verdicts.reading: Iraq's government faces political tests in 2009 (elections, US withdrawal) that threaten unity and stability.
verdicts.mainstream_test: In 2009 the tests produced documented instability or threatened the country's unity.
verdicts.reason: Provincial elections and the US pullback from cities went ahead and the country stayed united, but mass-casualty bombings hit government ministries in August and October 2009 (155 killed on 25 October, deadliest since 2007) and threatened Maliki's standing. The risk materialised in part.

evidence.title: 25 October 2009 Baghdad bombings (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: 155 killed at the Justice Ministry and provincial council; 120 killed in August bombings nearby; political impact on Maliki before 2010 elections.

evidence.title: 2009 Venezuelan constitutional referendum (Wikipedia)

verdicts.reading: Rising narco violence and corruption scandals keep raising doubts about Mexico's anti-crime strategy in 2009.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Drug-related violence rose in 2009 and the strategy was publicly questioned.
verdicts.reason: Drug-related deaths rose 22% from 6,290 (2008) to 7,724 (2009); thousands of troops were sent to Ciudad Juarez, the world's most violent city; senior police officials were charged over cartel links.

evidence.title: Timeline of the Mexican drug war (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Deaths 6,290 in 2008 and 7,724 in 2009; troop surge to Juarez February 2009; corruption arrests of top police officials.

verdicts.reading: No war with Russia, but the Tymoshenko-Yushchenko feud divides Ukraine's government and hampers its crisis response in 2009.

evidence.title: 2008-2009 Ukrainian financial crisis (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Economy shrank about 15%; feud between Tymoshenko and Yushchenko hindered anti-crisis measures; IMF very worried in November 2009.

verdicts.reading: The secularist-Islamist struggle in Turkey becomes a serious obstacle to economic progress and the EU bid in 2009.

evidence.title: Accession of Turkey to the European Union (Wikipedia)
